recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16136; future review of Observation.focus modifier semantics should start from FHIR-37736 and FHIR-45259.
issue_request: FHIR-16136 was Published / Not Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked whether Observation.focus should be a modifier because ignoring focus could make an observation appear to be about the wrong entity. The accepted STU3 application clarified Observation.subject, requested subject/focus examples and documentation, and added a safety note rather than marking focus as a modifier at that time.
initial_application: The seed was applied by git-svn commit 8da41eb1e5b69c9ac8d6b759ba1c88e9d892b881, which updated the old Observation spreadsheet subject short name, definition, and comment, and by 19fc6ffc60591f5ab930855904c55bcdb2d7006e, which added the Observation.focus clinical safety checklist item. The migrated current source carries this through structuredefinition-Observation.xml, observation-notes.xml, and safety.html.
additional_context: Later final decisions changed the current modifier status: FHIR-16188 clarified the isModifier rule, FHIR-37736 made Observation.focus a modifier while clarifying related-person focus cases, and FHIR-45259 directly requested Observation.focus modifier treatment. FHIR-37736 and FHIR-45259 are already represented on the combined branch, so no duplicate related commits were published.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reverting Observation.focus to non-modifier would conflict with later Applied/Persuasive decisions, and adding more prose would duplicate existing StructureDefinition, Observation notes, and safety checklist guidance.
